{{Quote|We're using Y-wings because of their greater firepower. But they move like a sleepy Hutt, so watch it.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], during the [[Assault on Kile II]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>}}
The '''BTL Y-wing starfighter''' was a [[Starfighter/Legends|fighter]]-[[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] built by [[Koensayr Manufacturing/Legends|Koensayr Manufacturing]]. First used during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], then throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it was a mainstay of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] [[Alliance Starfighter Corps/Legends|Starfighter Corps]]. It was often used as an assault [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]] to attack enemy [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] directly in conjunction with the later [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighters]].

==Design==
{{Quote|They're the workhorses of this outfit, I can tell you that.|[[Tiree/Legends|Tiree]]|<ref name="Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope (novel)">[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novel]]</ref>}}
[[File:Ywing_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Y-wing [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]

Affectionately known as a "wishbone" to Rebel Alliance and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], the Y-wing [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was deployed as a fighter-bomber, designed to fight its way to its objective, deliver its payload of high explosives, and fight its way out again. Its weaponry included two [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], two [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], and two [[Proton torpedo/Legends|proton torpedo]] launchers. An [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]], such as an [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2 unit]], could be plugged into a socket behind the cockpit to act as a co-pilot and manage the ship's various systems.

The Y-wing was a resilient, well-[[Deflector shield/Legends|shielded]] craft, but was slow and ungainly compared to other Alliance fighters. Its deficiencies were partly compensated for by the heavy proton torpedo load it could carry, and its ability to paralyze craft with ion cannon fire without destroying them, a unique ability until the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing starfighter]] was introduced after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. In addition to the Rebel Alliance, many [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] defense forces, [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], and [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] fielded the craft.

The design had many flaws and required constant maintenance. The Y-wing was originally entirely sheathed in an aerodynamic, elegant fuselage, but its high-maintenance nature led to many aggravated maintenance crews getting fed up with constantly having to remove the superficial [[Hull/Legends|hull]] plating and disposing of it altogether. Due to this, many Y-wings had no hull plating (except on the cockpit), exposing the internals of the main hull. Pilots found that this lightened the frame and kept components cooler, noticeably boosting performance.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

In at least one Y-wing, special features were included which assisted in the event of crashing on the surface of a planet. Inflatable balloons were deployed which kept the ship afloat in case of a water landing, and the cockpit could be ejected from the rest of the ship and driven as its own vehicle. It is unknown whether this was a standard feature or a customization.<ref name="The Star Wars Holiday Special animated segment">''[[The Story of the Faithful Wookiee]]''</ref>

==Usage==
{{Quote|They've always gotten me home in one piece.|[[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm]]|<ref name="CCG Salm">{{CCG|set=Death Star II Limited|cardname=Colonel Salm}}</ref>}}
[[File:Original_Y-wing.jpg|thumb|left|280px|A relatively unscathed Y-wing with its hull plates still in place]]
Despite its shortcomings in speed and maneuverability compared to space superiority fighters such as the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] (or especially compared to interceptors like the [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|A-wing]]), the Y-wing was an extremely durable craft, with heavier armor and shielding making it a favorite among some Alliance pilots during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The Y-wing also had a larger [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedo]] magazine.

The Y-wing was not a sluggish fighter overall, as its speed and agility exceeded that of its intended replacement, the B-wing, but its lack of mobility meant that the Y-wing was not effective as a space superiority fighter. When properly used by such commanders as [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grisserno]] and [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm]], Y-wings would accelerate towards their [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] targets, relying on their gunners and wingmates in X-wing starfighters and A-wing interceptors to distract enemy fighters and the enemy ships' [[Gunner/Legends|gunners]]. This would allow the Y-wings and B-wings to focus their fire on capital ships.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> This tactic was similar to the [[A-wing Slash/Legends|A-wing Slash]], which involved solely X-wings and A-wings.

==Models==
There were three common designs of Y-wing, one used during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and two during the height of the Galactic Civil War, as well as six less common variants.

===BTL-B Y-wing===
{{Main|BTL-B Y-wing starfighter}}
[[File:BTL-BYwing-SWE.png|thumb|left|180px|BTL-B Y-wing]]
The first known model was the '''BTL-B''', which served the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] during the Clone Wars. Unlike its successor designs, the BTL-B model had a full [[Hull/Legends|hull]] covering on both the primary fuselage and engines. A bubble-turret, which swivelled 360 degrees, provided a clear view for the [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]] of the surrounding space. The ship was designed to operate mainly as a bomber and the Republic used them well in this capacity.<ref name="SW:TCWtv">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''</ref> On later models, this bubble feature was replaced with a turret operated from within the main cockpit.<ref name="CCS" />

===BTL-S3 Y-wing===
{{Main|BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends}}

<div style="float:right">[[File:Btl-s3.jpg|thumb|left|180px|BTL-S3 Y-wing]]</div>

The '''BTL-S3''' was a two-man strike fighter, and was the most common Y-wing configuration.<ref name="The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> The weapons systems officer typically operated the ion cannon turret when needed.<ref name="Star Wars Sourcebook">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref>

[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] used this variant on his mission to [[Panna/Legends|Panna]] in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="Star Wars Holiday Special">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> as did [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] on their journey to the [[Circarpous system/Legends|Circarpous system]].<ref name="Splinter of the Mind's Eye">''[[Splinter of the Mind's Eye]]''</ref>

Many Y-wings of this variant were modified to become the '''[[BTL-S3B Y-wing starfighter|S3B]]''' variant, with defensive rapid-fire blaster turrets replacing the ion cannon turret,<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" /> and [[particle cannon]]s replacing the dual laser cannons on the nose.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront II">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> These Y-wings were used as heavy [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] destroyers, and were eventually phased out by the new B-wing starfighters.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" />

===BTL-A4 Y-wing===
{{Main|BTL-A4 Y-wing starfighter/Legends}}

[[File:Ywing.jpg|thumb|left|180px|BTL-A4 Y-wing]]

The BTL-A4 was a one-man version of the S3, which removed the gunner position and locked the overhead ion cannon in a forward-facing position. Shield strength was also reduced to boost engine speed. It was commonly used by pirate, mercenary, and private defense forces, and therefore was also used by the early [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] as the primary starfighter for bombing and disabling roles. However, the lack of a gunner and reduced shields typically proved a liability and made the A4 unpopular among pilots. Notably, only one A4 fighter from the Alliance's [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]] survived the attack on the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star]] at the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="Essential Guide to Warfare" />

As the BTL-S3 became the primary Y-wing variant of the Rebel forces, the A4 was still kept in many units as a supplementary craft. However, [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red]] and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadrons]] favored<ref name="X-W">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> the A4 variant of the Y-wing and used it with distinction in several climactic battles, such as the Battle of Yavin, the capture of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Death Star II plans|plans]] from the Imperial freighter ''[[Suprosa]]'',<ref name="Shadows of the Empire (novel)">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''</ref> and the subsequent [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].

===BTL-A4 Y-wing "LongProbe"===
{{Main|BTL-A4 LP "Longprobe"}}
<div style="float:right">[[File:Y-wing_LP.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A BTL-A4 Y-wing LongProbe]]</div>
An additional (though less common) BTL-A4 variant known as the "'''LongProbe'''," designated '''BTL-A4 (LP)''', was equipped with a [[Navigation computer/Legends|nav computer]], backup hyperdrive, advanced scanners, and an extended fuel supply in place of the weapons systems officer.<ref name="SOTG07" /> While this was not enough to make it into a true scout craft, its heavy armament gave it a better chance of survival and allowed it to occasionally cause damage to the targets it was scouting.<ref name="SOTG07" /> The LongProbe was used primarily for long-range scouting missions.<ref name="Rebel Alliance Sourcebook">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> On such missions, LongProbes operated in recon teams known as LongProbe Y-wing Recon Teams. One such team was sent to [[Alashan]] to check a Rebel [[Archaeology/Legends|archeological]] dig that failed to report back.<ref name="World of Fire!">{{StoryCite|story=World of Fire!|book=Star Wars Weekly 107}}</ref> In contrast with most other Y-wings, this variant was considered too valuable to remove from active duty by the New Republic.<ref name="CTD">''[[Cracken's Threat Dossier]]''</ref>

===BTL-S3 Courier variant===
[[File:YWingCourier.png|thumb|left|180px|BTL-S3 Y-wing Courier]]
[[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] utilized specially modified Y-wings for long-range courier duty. This variant of the BTL-S3 had no ion cannons (which were removed for baggage space), a larger main cockpit area able to carry up to five people, and a special canopy split down the middle for rapid embarking or disembarking of a passenger during brief landings. This canopy also allowed a passenger to bail out at high altitude and paraglide to their destination. The customization was rare enough that no special designation was created for these modified Y-wings.<ref name="SOTG07" /> Some of the last Rebel soldiers to [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|evacuate]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] used Y-wings of this type.<ref name="Marvel Star Wars #78">[[Star Wars (1977) 78|''Star Wars'' (1977) 78]]</ref><ref name="Star Wars: Visionaries - Entrenched">{{StoryCite|story=Entrenched|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> The variant was used by Princess Leia and Luke Skywalker on missions to [[Velmor/Legends|Velmor]] and [[Ventooine/Legends|Ventooine]].<ref name="Marvel Star Wars #49">[[Star Wars (1977) 49|''Star Wars'' (1977) 49]]</ref> A Y-wing modified similarly by [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]] was used by Skywalker while he was working for the [[Senate Planetary Intelligence Network]] and helping the [[Adventures of a Jedi Prince|Jedi Prince]] [[Ken]].<ref name="Prophets of the Dark Side">[[Prophets of the Dark Side (novel)|''Prophets of the Dark Side'']]</ref>

===Light Y-wing===
The [[Light Y-wing]] was a light [[Bomber/Legends|bomber]], which lacked the support pylons on the engine.<ref name="SW:GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

===Heavy Y-wing===
The [[Heavy Y-wing]] was a bomber with heavier ordnance and four engine pods.<ref name="SW:GB" />

===Y-Wing Scout Bomber===
The [[Y-wing scout bomber/Legends|Y-wing Scout Bomber]] was a variant developed and deployed during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Star Wars: The Clone Wars toy line">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (toy line)|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' toy line]]</ref>

==History==
[[File:Btlbywing.png|thumb|right|250px|An early Y-wing (with [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] in the background) in use by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]]]
Koensayr Manufacturing designed the Y-wing for use by the Galactic Republic in the Clone Wars, and although the BTL-B model saw combat, as flown by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and a group of clone troopers to disable the [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']],<ref name="SW:TCWtv" /> the more commonly known BTL-S3 came later. The Y-wing also served during the [[Battle of Ryloth/Legends|Battle of Ryloth]], in the [[Battle of Kamino/Legends|Battle of Kamino]] to stop [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] frigates, and at the [[Battle of Malastare/Legends|Battle of Malastare]] to help secure the [[Electro-proton bomb/Legends|electro-proton bomb]] by [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|Vulture Droids]].

When the Galactic Empire declined to buy the design, Koensayr began selling to various parties, and Y-wings found their way into pirate and mercenary forces; thus the fighter ended up with Rebel groups early in the Galactic Civil War.<ref name="SOTG07" /> BTL-S3 Y-wings were in service at least as early as [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], and it was a critical vessel in the Rebellion's early days, bearing the brunt of all of its early space battles with the Empire. The Rebels lost more Y-wings in the Galactic Civil War than any other fighter, due to the simple fact that they flew more Y-wings than any other fighter.

[[File:Ywing_targeting_comp.png|thumb|left|200px|The [[Targeting computer/Legends|targeting computer]] on a Y-wing]]
Even after the introduction of the X-wing, which largely succeeded it in most roles, it continued to serve as an important part of the Alliance arsenal. The Y-wing was best suited for heavy assault missions due to its larger warhead payload and stronger hull and shields, while the X-wing and A-wing were more focused on dealing with enemy starfighters.

It was also invaluable for disabling craft since it was for a time the only predominant Alliance starfighter with ion cannons. The more heavily armed and more advanced B-wing was supposed to supplant the Y-wing for such assault and capture missions. However, the Y-wing still retained an edge over the B-wing in armor. As the Y-wing was a proven design and easier to pilot than the B-wing, which was available in limited numbers, the Y-wing continued to play a role as late as the Battle of Endor.

By the time of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]] against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], Y-wings were relegated to planetary defense duties, leaving attack missions to X-wings, A-wings, and B-wings. Their age made them more difficult to repair, and many expected them to leave service as newer fighters came into production.

[[File:Ywing_SOCcover.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A group of Y-wings over [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]]]]

One exception to this general demotion of Y-wings from active duty was the BTL-A4 "Longprobe" scout, which filled a vital niche in the reconnaissance role. Although partially replaced by the [[T-65BR X-wing reconnaissance starfighter|T-65BR X-wing]] variant, these fighters were considered too valuable to withdraw. Instead, they were upgraded, extending their usefulness until the final years of the long conflict with the Empire, if not beyond.<ref name="CTD" />

Additionally, stubborn old Y-wings, in varying states of repair, were still found throughout the galaxy long after the Galactic Civil War. During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Fian/Legends|Fia]] of the [[Galantos Guard]] employed Y-wings in defense of their homeworld, though pilots of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] referred to the starfighters as "old" and "clumsy."<ref name="NJO FH1 R">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant]]''</ref> Other Y-wings found their way into private ownership and continued to fly during the [[Second Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Betrayal">''[[Legacy of the Force: Betrayal]]''</ref><ref name="Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref> In [[44 ABY]], an antique Y-wing was docked at [[Skifter Station|Skifter]] [[Space station/Legends|space station]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] [[Kuratooine]].<ref name="X:MK">''[[X-Wing: Mercy Kill]]''</ref>

Famous Y-wing pilots included [[Jon Vander/Legends|Jon Vander]], who led [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadron]] during the Battle of Yavin; [[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Keyan Farlander]], the only surviving member from Gold Squadron in the attack; [[Davish Krail/Legends|Davish Krail]], who had flown them for five years; and [[Horton Salm/Legends|Horton Salm]], one of the New Republic's foremost Y-wing pilots. Salm led the Alliance's [[Gray Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gray Squadron]] at the Battle of Endor, surviving the run through the second Death Star's superstructure, later leading [[Aggressor Wing]] through the [[Battle of Brentaal IV (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Brentaal IV]], which saw him promoted to the rank of [[General/Legends|general]]; he continued to command the Aggressors during the [[evacuation of Ciutric]].

==Behind the scenes==
''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' erroneously refers to the BTL-A4 Y-wing starfighter as the "BLT-A4 Y-wing." This was corrected in ''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''.

Because of the conflict in continuity between the Y-wing's appearance in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|the ''Clone Wars'' series]] and its history prior to this series, Jason Fry attempted to combine the different sources in the Y-wing's sensor profile in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="JLT10">{{Tumblr|subdomain=jasonfry|url=post/24614452839/eg-to-warfare-endnotes-pt-10|name=Jason Fry's Dorkery|text=EG to Warfare: Endnotes Pt. 10}}</ref>
